summary: OAuth token refresh intermittently fails for Private deployment when egress proxy downgrades TLS and VPCE connection toggles
description:
Issue summary:
Acropolis Financial reports intermittent failures during OAuth token refreshes from Redwood control plane to their external identity provider (IdP). Failures correlate with short VPCE egress path changes and an on-prem transparent HTTP/TLS inspection proxy that sometimes downgrades TLS parameters. When the failure occurs, Redwood control-plane auth attempts return 502/504 or TLS handshake errors which cause model-serving auth refresh to fail and subsequent 401s for control-plane operations.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing degraded model serving at peak times for a subset (~5-10%) of requests that require control-plane token refresh.
- Visible effects: transient 401s from serving nodes, increased retry loops, and spikes in error-trace alerts for model pull and rekey flows.

Observed behavior (from customer traces and control-plane logs):
- Errors: repeated TLS handshake timeouts and TLS alert 40 (handshake_failure) observed on egress connections to idp.acropolis.example.com.
- When TLS handshake succeeds, server often negotiates TLS1.2 with ECDHE and then token POST returns 200. When handshake fails, the client logs show TLS1.3 ClientHello not answered or connection reset mid-handshake.
- Failure window aligns with VPCE route update events (tenant reports brief route churn when their SD-WAN rebalances across two transit gateways).
- Retry pattern: Redwood SDK retries 3x with exponential backoff, then surfaces 502 to serving layer.

Environment and constraints:
- Private deployment using VPCE to connect to Redwood control plane and outbound internet via customer's egress appliance (transparent proxy + TLS inspection).
- Customer uses a corporate proxy that performs TLS inspection and may rewrite TLS extensions (alpn/cipher order) and occasionally strips TLS1.3 key_share extension, triggering server to reject handshake.
- VPCE configuration: aws-vpce interface endpoint clustered across two AZs; transient routing/next-hop changes reported by customer during SD-WAN rebalance.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Deploy a model-serving job pinned to v1.3.2 on private cluster.
2) Generate load that triggers frequent control-plane token refreshes (short token TTL configured for testing).
3) Induce SD-WAN rebalance or toggle egress path to force VPCE route switchover.
4) Observe token refresh failures in control-plane logs and 401s at serving nodes.

Initial triage notes:
- Hypothesis A: Transparent proxy strips/rewrites TLS1.3 key_share or PSK extensions causing handshake failures with IdP.
- Hypothesis B: VPCE route churn causes TCP connection reuse to a different proxy appliance that has a different TLS config (ALPN/cipher), yielding intermittent failures.
- Hypothesis C: Client-side reuse of TLS session tickets across different egress NAT/IPs (post-churn) leads to server rejecting resume, resulting in hard handshake failures.

Logs and references:
- Sample control-plane egress logs (redacted): "tls_handshake_error: alert 40 / client_hello unsupported extension" (timestamps align with route updates).
- Customer packet capture (redacted) showing ClientHello with TLS1.3 + key_share then RST after 1s.
- Relevant dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/tenant/Acropolis/token-refresh-errors

Requested from customer/support team:
- Packet capture (pcap) for a failure window (provided).
- Exact VPCE flow logs and any transient route updates timestamps (requested).
- Confirmation whether proxy performs SNI rewrite, TLS interception with custom CA, or terminates TLS for certain destinations.

Expected behavior:
- Token refreshes should succeed despite VPCE route changes or proxy presence; TLS inspection appliances should allow TLS1.3 handshakes (or gracefully fall back) without causing handshake_failure alerts.

Next steps proposed by Support/SRE:
1) Ask customer to whitelist idp.acropolis.example.com (or allow passthrough) for TLS inspection to test if that removes failures.
2) If passthrough not possible, request proxy vendor logs and TLS policy details (cipher suites, extensions removed).
3) Add short-term mitigation in our control-plane: increase token refresh retry count and jitter, and avoid TLS session ticket reuse across aggressive IP changes by forcing fresh TLS handshake when egress local IP changes detected.
4) Correlate VPCE/flow logs timestamps with captured handshakes to prove route-change causality.

Customer-provided artifacts attached (links):
- pcap: https://acropolis-secure-files.example.com/sup-893214/failure-window.pcap
- vpce-flow-logs: provided in support ticket thread
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (reporter): Customer opened after multiple production incidents; initial symptom is token refresh 502 followed by serving 401s. Provided pcap and flow logs.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Diego Alvarez (Support): Assigned for triage. Asked customer whether proxy can bypass TLS inspection for idp domain and requested exact VPCE route-change timestamps and SD-WAN event logs.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Customer (Acropolis NetOps): Confirmed proxy performs TLS inspection using a corporate CA and may strip key_share in some appliances; provided SD-WAN change log showing route flaps at 2026-03-10T08:58:23Z and 09:04:10Z.
2026-03-10 15:45 - SRE Oncall (Lena Park): Observed matching TLS alert 40 in control-plane egress logs at same timestamps. Noted client-side TLS stack indicates ClientHello offered TLS1.3 key_share.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Diego Alvarez: Requested customer run quick test to allow passthrough for idp host for 30 minutes to confirm mitigation. Also proposed a short term control-plane change: force new TLS handshake when local egress IP changes to avoid reusing session ticket with a different NAT mapping.

2026-03-11 12:01 - Customer (Acropolis NetOps): Performed passthrough test for 20 minutes; during that window token refresh errors dropped to zero. After reverting to inspection, failures resumed. Customer confirms proxy does alter TLS extensions.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented a canary change in staging to avoid TLS session resumption across egress-IP-change and increased retry jitter. Observed reduction in replicated token refresh 502s in staging under simulated route changes.

2026-03-12 12:10 - SRE (Lena Park): Recommended we track as a known interoperability issue with transparent TLS-inspection appliances that remove TLS1.3 extensions. Suggested documenting mitigation steps in private-deploy runbook and notify Customer Success.

2026-03-12 15:00 - Diego Alvarez: Action items created: (1) provide customer runbook for whitelisting IdP or configuring proxy to preserve TLS1.3 key_share; (2) schedule change to production control-plane to enable egress-IP-change handshake avoidance and extended retry jitter (targeting 2026-03-18 canary).
resolution_notes: Mitigation validated with customer: temporary passthrough eliminated failures. Implemented staging change to avoid TLS session resume across egress IP change and increased retry jitter. Next: schedule production canary and provide customer runbook with proxy configuration options. Pending customer confirmation of proxy vendor capability or whitelist rollout.
